name: Purchase history
summary: Invoice-line purchases from distributors, manufacturers or local vendors: what was bought, by which location, in what pack, at what price, under which deal.

goals.label: Check what I'm charged
goals.desc: I'd check every line against your contract terms

goals.label: Find savings
goals.desc: I'd find where you paid more than your own best price

goals.label: Compare vendors or rebid
goals.desc: I'd build a clean item list with yearly volumes

goals.label: Explain or share it
goals.desc: I'd write a guide for the next person

questions.prompt: Are these {rows} lines every purchase for the dates they cover, across all your locations and vendors?
questions.why: Totals, savings and rebate estimates are only right on complete data.

fact.statement: Coverage of these purchase lines, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: How do your deals show up against the {rows:unit_price} prices in {role:unit_price}? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Taken off on the invoice line

questions.why: It decides whether a saving is new or already taken, and whether rebates stack on top.

fact.statement: How deals show up against {role:unit_price}, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: There are {count:pack} different pack sizes, for example {values:pack}. How should I compare prices?

options.label: Per base unit
options.desc: Every pack in its base unit

questions.why: Different pack sizes can make the same product look cheaper or dearer than it is.

fact.statement: Prices are compared on this basis, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: {role:ext_price} adds up to {sum:ext_price} on {rows:ext_price} lines. Which of these should count in spend? Pick all that apply.
questions.recommend_basis: Spend analysis normally nets credits and returns against purchases; leaving them out overstates spend.
questions.why: Credits, fees and internal transfers change totals and unit prices, and mixing them in silently skews every comparison.

fact.statement: The owner said these count in spend: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: There are {count:item_id} different {role:item_id} codes and {count:mfr_item_id} different {role:mfr_item_id} values. Should lines with the same {role:mfr_item_id} count as one product, even under different {role:item_id} codes?
questions.why: Code changes break price history and can hide a price increase.

fact.statement: Lines with the same {role:mfr_item_id} under different {role:item_id} codes, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: Are any of these vendors on a contract or buying-group program? What kind of deal is it?

options.label: I have a contract price file

questions.why: Without your terms the audit can only compare you to yourself.

fact.statement: Vendor pricing terms, per the owner: {answer_labels}. {answer_text}

questions.prompt: Which rebate programs pay back on these purchases? Pick all that apply.

options.label: A buying group
options.desc: A GPO or buying group program

questions.why: Rebates are earned on the line but paid months later, so the audit needs to know which buys should earn them.

fact.statement: Rebate programs on these purchases, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: Your {count:location} locations include {values:location}. Can each one buy the same items at the best price found here?

options.label: Yes, one program for all
options.desc: Any location can buy any item at the best price

questions.why: A saving only counts where a site can actually switch to the lower price.

fact.statement: Whether every location can buy at the best price found, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

questions.prompt: Where do your portion sizes and recipe yields live?

options.label: A recipe file
options.desc: A recipe file of its own

options.label: I'll type them for top items

questions.why: A plate cost needs how much of each item goes on the plate and how much is lost to trim.

fact.statement: Portion sizes and yields, per the owner: {answer_labels}.

outputs.title: Contract audit
outputs.pitch: Contract audit: every line checked against your agreed price, markup and rebate terms, with overcharges listed by vendor and invoice, ready for credit requests.

outputs.title: Savings map
outputs.pitch: Savings map: items where one location paid more than the best price in this data for the same product, with the gap at your volumes.

outputs.title: Bid pack
outputs.pitch: Bid pack: a clean item list with specs, pack sizes and yearly volumes to send vendors for quotes. It carries no prices, no terms and no notes from this file.

outputs.title: Plate cost
outputs.pitch: Plate cost: connect a recipe or menu file on {role:item_id} and price every portion from what you actually paid.

outputs.title: Guide for the next owner
outputs.pitch: Guide for the next owner: a plain page on what this file is, what one row is, how prices, credits and fees work here, and what to watch for.

outputs.title: App blueprint
outputs.pitch: App blueprint: a purchasing monitor that reads each week's invoices, prices every line per comparable unit, and flags price jumps, off-contract items and missing credits before you pay.

gotchas.say: Lines are priced per {values:uom}, so a case price and a pound price cannot be compared directly.
{role:catch_weight} holds actual shipped weight. Catch-weight items are ordered by the case but billed by the pound, so quantity times price will not match the line total on those lines.
{role:ext_price} has negative lines: credits, returns or mispicks. Left in, they pull average prices down; left out, spend is overstated.
No vendor column was found. A distributor export usually covers one vendor, whose name sits in the file name or a title row.
{role:allowance} is shown on the line, so the invoice price may already reflect that deal. Counting it again as a saving would double it.
{role:rebate} is earned on these buys but usually paid later, often quarterly, so it does not lower the invoice price on these lines.
Distributors reassign item codes when products change, so {role:mfr_item_id} is often a steadier key for price history than {role:item_id}.
{role:item_id} is blank on some lines. Fee, credit and special-order lines often carry no item code.
{role:location} holds short codes such as {values:location}. One of them may be a commissary or central kitchen, whose lines are internal transfers rather than purchases.
{role:contract_price} is the agreed price, but market-priced items such as proteins and produce can float week to week under the same contract.
Other files may name the same product by the distributor's item code, the manufacturer's number or the GTIN, so matches are checked on more than one key.

graph.sentence: Dots are vendors, locations, categories and top items. Lines show who supplies what and where it goes. Bigger means more spend.

rules.basis: Distributor prices change weekly on market-priced items and at the end of each lock period on fixed-price items.
Rebate rates are set per program year.
